To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the reactions of the Cu/Ti/Silicon Dioxide structures at the temperature range from 200 to the 700 degrees Celsius were studied for various titanium thicknesses.

Ti reactions with Cu and SiO2 in Cu/Ti structures were affected by the oxygen content in unreacted Ti and that the diffusion barrier properties of Ti for Cu were reduced by an increased thickness of Ti.
Ti reactions are strongly affected by the oxygen content in Ti films, and that the Ti reactions are also strongly influenced by the diffusion barrier properties of the SiO2 layer.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the effects of the oxygen content in Ti films on the reactions of Cu/Tisystems upon annealing, and the results can be used to design a suitable diffusion barrier for Cu metallization.
the effects of the dissolved oxygen content in Ti on its reactions with Cu and SiO2 upon annealing.
the effect of oxygen in the Ti layer on Ti reactions in the Cu/Ti/Sio2 system.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the Ti reactions in the Cu/Ti/Sio2 system were affected significantly by the oxygen content in Ti films.
the reactions of Cu/TiT/SiO2 were governed by the oxygen content in Ti films, which is a function of the Ti thickness.

the oxygen concentration in the Ti layer plays a critical role in the reaction sequences of the Cu/Ti/SuO2 system upon annealing, which is the result of the interplay of the thermodynamic and kinetic effects.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
a thicker Ti layer is not necessarily beneficial to the diffusion barrier properties of Ti/SiO2 in Cu/Ti structures.
the Ti reactions are significantly affected by the dissolved oxygen in the Ti layer.
the oxygen in the Ti film is a key factor that controls the reaction sequences of Ti in the Cu/Ti/Sio2 system upon annealing.
The main takeaway from our work is that

the oxygen content in unreacted Ti films can be used as a measure of the extent of the Ti reactions, and that it can be employed to optimize the thickness of the Ti layer for a desired reaction sequence.
the oxygen dissolved in Ti films plays a crucial role in determining the Ti reaction sequences, and thus, the diffusion barrier properties of Ti films for Cu metallization.
oxygen in the Ti films is an important factor in the Ti–Cu reaction, and it is necessary to control the oxygen concentration in the Ti films to improve the diffusion barrier properties of Ti.
